states.tradition: Mangalagiri sarees and fabrics (Nizam border with inverted checks and dots; checked body)
states.caution: The 'Nizam border' name references Hyderabad's Nizam patronage and the gopuram points reference the Narasimha temples of Mangalagiri (guntur.ap.gov.in); keep framing as 'inspired by Mangalagiri handloom' and avoid using the GI name on outputs.

sources.title: GI Application 198 - Mangalagiri Sarees and Fabrics

states.tradition: Apatani textiles (banded shawls, three-band skirts, lozenge-row jackets)
states.caution: The jilan/jilang pulye and jig-jiro are priestly ceremonial shawls said to carry supernatural power and worn at Myoko, Murung and Subu rituals; the jikhe tarii and certain skirts mark social position and ceremonial status. Frame any design as 'inspired by Apatani band and lozenge weaving', never as a reproduction of a named priestly shawl. The GI is held by a producer company (Zeet Zeero), not the community as a whole.

sources.title: GI Application 808 - Arunachal Pradesh Apatani Textile Product
The Style and Motifs in the Art of Arunachal Pradesh (D. K. Durah)

states.tradition: Gamosa red-on-white border and motif band
states.caution: The gamosa is a strong symbol of Assamese identity, used in Bihu, as a mark of respect, and in religious/satra contexts (Gossain gamosa); treat with respect, say 'inspired by gamosa borders', and do not sell or label outputs as GI 'Asomiya Gamosa'. The 2019-2023 GI process involved disputes between applicant bodies; cite the Directorate of Handloom & Textiles as proprietor.

sources.title: Press Release No. 64/2023: CM Dr. Sarma receives GI Registration Certification for Assamese Gamosa

Cotton and Silk Weaving of Assam

states.tradition: Madhubani (Mithila) painting - double-line borders and hatched fills
states.caution: Kohbar (nuptial chamber) and tantric imagery are ritual; godna-style is specific to the Dusadh community; deities and epics dominate figurative work. Keep to abstract borders and fills 'inspired by Mithila line work'; do not reproduce kohbar diagrams or deity figures; avoid implying caste-style attribution.

states.tradition: Bastar wooden craft (incised and fire-branded geometric ornament on doors, combs and panels)
states.caution: Memorial pillars (Madia khamb) and ghotul doors have ritual/funerary meaning; use 'inspired by Bastar incised ornament' and do not reproduce ancestor-pillar iconography or ghotul-specific symbols. Attribute to Bastar Adivasi communities generically rather than to a named clan.

sources.title: From combs to icons: The trajectory of wood crafts in Bastar (Hindi)
Wood craft tradition of Bastar (module overview, Hindi)

states.caution: Garment of a historically marginalised tribal community; The Better India documents caste stigma attached to wearing it. Colours carried social meaning (blue/lilac for widows). Attribute to the Kunbi/Gawda communities of Goa and use 'inspired by Kunbi check'; do not use 'Kunbi' as a brand name.

sources.title: Orientation programme on revival of Kunbi handloom weaving held (press release, 3 April 2023)
In a Tucked-Away Goa Village, Women Are Restoring Pride to a Saree That Carried Generations of Stigma
Wrapped in cotton: the sarees Goa wears

states.caution: Strong ritual/wedding associations (gharchola is the Hindu/Jain wedding sari; Bishnoi yellow-with-red-dot mantles mark motherhood of sons). Technique is shared with Rajasthan, MP, Tamil Nadu and Sindh; two separate GIs name Jamnagar and Kutch. Say 'inspired by bandhani dot fields'; do not claim either GI name.

sources.title: GI Application 756 - Kutch Bandhani of Gujarat

states.tradition: Phulkari and Bagh counted-thread embroidery (Haryana practice: Rohtak, Hisar, Hansi, Ambala)
states.caution: Dowry/bridal textiles made by grandmothers and mothers (chope, vari-da-bagh); darshan dwar pieces are made for Sikh gurdwaras. Shared across Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Pakistani Punjab; do not claim a Haryana-only origin. GI-protected name: label output 'inspired by phulkari/bagh geometry'. Note the GSA Archives record of a deliberate 'purple stripe to spoil symmetry' (humility convention): perfect symmetry is a verifier convenience, not a cultural requirement.

sources.title: GI Journal No. 12 (01-01-2006), Phulkari specification (POST form, DocumentPath '27/27 - GI - Journal Copy - 01-01-2006.pdf')

states.caution: Border motifs include stylised Buddhist symbols and the five colours carry element symbolism (water, earth, fire, ether, air) in the GI description; use 'inspired by Kinnauri shawl borders' and avoid claiming religious meaning for generated tiles. Kinnauri borders are also woven onto Kullu shawls, so attribute to Kinnaur, not Kullu, when the geometric border is the subject.

sources.title: GIs of H.P. (HP Patent Information Centre, HIMCOSTE)
Kinnauri Shawl - Geographical Index in the Public Domain

states.tradition: Sohrai-Khovar wall painting (Kamalban intersecting-circle lotus forest, comb-cut and glyptic styles)
states.caution: Ritual art: Sohrai protects cattle and home from evil spirits; Khovar decorates the nuptial chamber; Pashupati, Mother Goddess and ancestor (Purkha) figures are sacred. Use only the abstract compass-circle, triple-line and dot-row vocabulary; never render Pashupati, ancestor figures or Shadi Chowk itself. Credit the women painters of Hazaribagh (GI holder is a women's cooperative) and name communities collectively.

sources.title: GI Application 658 - Sohrai-Khovar Painting (record and 'GI - Journal Copy - 10-01-2020' = GI Journal No. 129, pp. 28-33)
Sohrai - The Wall Art Of Jharkhand

diwali_tie.claim: Asia InCH describes Sohrai as a post-harvest festival observed the day after Diwali and identifies domestic wall murals as its primary visual expression.

states.caution: Many motifs are temple/ritual objects (gopura, tulsi vrindavan, palanquin); the craft is a women's domestic tradition and a GI held by a state corporation with individual women as authorised users. Prefer abstract lattice/zigzag motifs and label outputs 'inspired by Kasuti'.

sources.title: World Embroidery Day: Discovering Kasuti, A Hidden Gem From Karnataka

states.caution: Onam ritual welcoming King Mahabali; the rings are popularly linked to deities (Kerala Tourism: 'believed to represent ten deities'); only natural flowers are traditionally allowed. Keep outputs abstract (rings and sectors), avoid deity figures, and say 'inspired by Onam pookalam'.

Family craft of specific Khatri households (Bagh Printers Association); women of the family traditionally do not print; labour is Bhil Adivasi. GI name protected. Say 'inspired by Bagh print geometry'. Avoid claiming links to Bagh cave paintings as fact (tourism-sourced claim).

sources.title: GI Application 98 - Bagh Prints of Madhya Pradesh
Hand Block Printing of Bagh, Madhya Pradesh
Bagh Prints from Madhya Pradesh (Dastkari Haat Samiti)
The heritage weave of Maheshwar and the prints of Bagh

states.caution: Ritual art: the chauk/Devchauk and Lagnachauk are sacred marriage paintings (dnh.gov.in: 'The painting is sacred and without it, the marriage cannot take place'); the goddess figure is painted in white as sacred. Use 'inspired by Warli geometry' and avoid rendering deity figures (Palghat) or calling output 'Warli art'. GI-protected name held by the Adivasi Yuva Seva Sangh; attribute to the Warli community, and note the tradition is shared with Gujarat and Dadra & Nagar Haveli.

sources.title: The enduring tribal artistry of Maharashtra: Warli paintings
Warli artists from the community painting the museum exterior (MTDC Palghar Lok Itihas Sangrahalaya)

states.tradition: Moirang Phee / Moirang Pheejin stepped-triangle border
states.caution: The motif derives from Pakhangba, a Meitei deity, and the cloth was royal tribute and is worn at Lai Haraoba and weddings; present it as 'inspired by the Moirang Pheejin stepped-triangle border' and avoid claiming religious meaning. Historically tied to the Thongkapam family lineage of weavers.

GI held by Bethany Society, Tura, facilitated by the Meghalaya Department of Handloom & Textiles; the muikron 'eye' is an auspicious symbol. Garo society is matrilineal and the Dakmanda is formal women's wear. Frame as 'inspired by the Garo muikron nested-diamond border'. GI journal states the textile is woven in acrylic today; HEPC mentions cotton, so avoid fibre claims.

GI held by the Government of Mizoram on behalf of weavers. Worn at Chapchar Kut, Cheraw dance and weddings, where it signals close kinship to the bride. Use 'inspired by Mizo Puanchei stripe order'; do not sell or label output as Puanchei.

sources.title: GI application 583 Mizo Puanchei (Form GI-1 and Statement of Case)
5 Mizo traditional shawls get GI tag

states.tradition: Chakhesang shawls (banded Naga shawls with square-row centres)
states.caution: Strong caution. Chakhesang shawls are GI-protected and community-owned; the Chakhesang Women Welfare Society sued a designer and TRIFED in 2020 over misuse. Many shawls encode earned status (Thupikhu/Hapidasa for Feast-of-Merit couples), are gendered (Rira men, Rura women), and some are reserved for funerals; wearing an unearned shawl is taboo. Never reproduce a named shawl's identity or its figurative motifs (mithun, elephant, spear, shield); generate only abstract band-and-square compositions 'inspired by Chakhesang band geometry'. Red dyeing is traditionally restricted to elder women.

sources.title: How the Chakhesang Naga community weaves a world of meaning into a shawl
In Nagaland, women weave through challenges
Nagaland GI Handloom Products - Chakhesang Shawls

states.tradition: Sambalpuri Bandha (ikat) - saktapar chequerboard body and rudraksha border
states.caution: Gitagovinda cloths have ritual use at the Jagannath temple; avoid scripts/verses. Conch, chakra and lotus are sacred motifs; keep generated patterns to checks, diamonds, stars, waves and dots. Shared ikat family across India and Asia; say 'inspired by Sambalpuri saktapar checks', not 'Sambalpuri'.

sources.title: GI Application 208 - Sambalpuri Bandha Saree & Fabrics (record and 'GI - Journal Copy - 11-01-2012' = GI Journal No. 44)

states.caution: Bridal and ritual textiles (chope from the grandmother, vari-da-bagh for the daughter-in-law, darshan dwar for gurdwaras); shared across Indian and Pakistani Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan. GI-protected: label output 'inspired by phulkari/bagh'. Credit women artisans; the craft was disrupted by Partition and is being revived by self-help groups and the Punjab government. Some makers deliberately break symmetry (GSA record), so perfect symmetry is a verifier choice.

sources.title: GI Journal No. 12 (01-01-2006), Phulkari specification (POST form, DocumentPath '27/27 - GI - Journal Copy - 01-01-2006.pdf')

states.caution: Craft identity of the Chhipa community; printed cloth historically signalled marital status and ethnic identity of wearer communities. Closely related to Sanganeri (separate GI) and to Ajrakh/dabu across Rajasthan-Gujarat-Sindh. Use 'inspired by Bagru block printing'; do not use the GI name on outputs.

states.caution: The dumpra is Lepcha men's identity dress and the sumok triangle refers to the Lepcha hat; attribute to the Lepcha (Rong) community, use 'inspired by Lepcha thara stripes', and do not present outputs as authentic Lepcha cloth. Also practised across the border in Darjeeling and Nepal.

Directorate of Handicrafts & Handloom, Gangtok (ICH archive entry)

states.caution: Kolam is a daily ritual offering (to Bhudevi / threshold deities) and is strongly gendered (women's practice); it is shared across Tamil-speaking regions and diaspora, so attribute it to the Tamil tradition rather than a single state. Avoid presenting generated outputs as ritual kolams; use 'inspired by the Tamil kolam tradition'. Do not combine with deity imagery.

states.caution: First Indian textile GI; the name is the registered property of the weavers' society, so outputs must say 'inspired by Pochampally ikat' and never use the name as a product label. The feathered edge is a hallmark of resist dyeing; a crisp raster is an inspiration, not a reproduction.

sources.title: Yarn Tie-Dye Weaving / Ikat of Pochampally, Telangana

states.caution: The Risa is given at a girl's coming-of-age (12-14), used in Garia puja and harvest festivals, gifted to honour guests, and tribe-specific motifs identify the wearer's community. Use 'inspired by Tripura Risa stripe symmetry' and do not label output with a specific tribe's named design (kwchak pali etc.).

states.tradition: Mughal pierced-stone jaali screens of Agra and Fatehpur Sikri
states.caution: These are Indo-Islamic funerary and religious monuments (Salim Chishti's dargah is an active Sufi shrine where pilgrims tie threads to the jalis). Use 'inspired by Mughal jaali geometry', never reproduce or name a specific shrine screen as the product. Jaali geometry is shared across the Islamic world; do not claim UP-exclusive origin. Many UP jalis (e.g. Taj cenotaph screen) are floral/inlaid rather than purely geometric; brief should target the geometric type.

sources.title: Jali (screen), carved sandstone, Agra, 19th century, copied from a late 16th century model (IS.1031-1883)

states.tradition: Aipan (Kumaoni ritual floor and wall painting)
states.caution: Ritual art tied to Hindu pujas, births, sacred-thread and marriage rites and to specific deities (Nav Durga, Saraswati, Shiva, Lakshmi); swastik is a sacred auspicious symbol here and must not be rendered in a way that resembles the Nazi hakenkreuz; avoid naming a specific deity chauki as a product; use 'inspired by Kumaoni aipan geometry'. GI-protected name 'Uttarakhand Aipan' should not be used as a product label. Made by women; attribute accordingly.

sources.title: GI Journal No. 138 (30-06-2020), Uttarakhand Aipan specification (POST form, DocumentPath '648/648 - GI - Journal Copy - 30-06-2020.pdf')

states.caution: Shared heritage of West Bengal and Bangladesh (Banglapedia is a Bangladeshi source); Katna's Muslim community deliberately avoids human and animal forms, so an abstract geometric brief is both respectful and accurate; say 'inspired by Bengal kantha counted stitching' rather than claiming a regional style.

sources.title: Katna's Kantha: Preserving a Tradition and Transforming Lives (Brinda Gill)

states.caution: The Nicobarese are a Scheduled Tribe in a restricted-access area and the GI is held by a tribal cooperative; any brief must say 'inspired by plaited pandanus mat structure' and must not claim to be a Nicobari mat or use the names Chatrai/Hileuoi as a product name. The mat has ceremonial use (serving food at festivals, hospitality). Do not extend this to other island communities: nothing from Jarawa, Sentinelese, Onge, Great Andamanese or Shompen material culture is proposed or appropriate.

sources.title: GI Application 1054 - Nicobari Mat (Chatrai / Hileuoi) of Andaman & Nicobar (record and 'GI - Journal Copy - 31-07-2024' = GI Journal No. 193, pp. 18-23)
Coconut Shell, Fibre & Stem Craft of Andaman & Nicobar
7 Indigenous Products of A & N Islands Receive Geographical Indication Tag

states.tradition: Phulkari (Chandigarh practice; honest fallback shared with Punjab and Haryana)
states.caution: Chandigarh has no craft tradition of its own older than the 1950s; be explicit that this is a shared Punjab/Haryana tradition hosted in the UT. Use 'inspired by phulkari' and do not imply a Chandigarh-specific style.

sources.title: Craft of India - Chandigarh: Phulkari (My City, My History project)

states.state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
states.caution: The marriage painting is sacred (dnh.gov.in: without it 'the marriage cannot take place'). The tradition originated in Maharashtra and is shared with Gujarat; attribute to the Warli community rather than to the UT administration. Avoid deity/horse motifs; use 'inspired by Warli geometry as practised around Silvassa'. Daman and Diu (the coastal districts) have no documented distinct geometric tradition in the sources found.

sources.title: Immerse yourself in the vibrant arts and handicrafts of Silvassa

states.tradition: Mughal sandstone and marble jaali screens of the Humayun's Tomb complex
states.caution: Funerary monuments (tombs of Humayun, Isa Khan, ~160 Mughal family members) adjacent to the living Sufi dargah of Nizamuddin Auliya; use 'inspired by Mughal jaali geometry', do not name or reproduce a specific tomb screen as a product. Geometric jaali vocabulary is pan-Islamic/pan-South-Asian; do not claim Delhi exclusivity. Conservation craftsmanship credit belongs to the stone carvers trained under AKTC/ASI.

Patterns derive from Islamic geometric tradition and are found in mosques and Sufi shrines (Khanqah-e-Moalla, Dastgir Sahib, Hazratbal); use 'inspired by Khatamband' and avoid implying sacred use. Attribute to Srinagar's Khatamband carpenters, not generic 'Islamic art'. Craft is GI-protected; do not label outputs as Khatamband.

sources.title: Application for registration of Khatamband (Form GI-1)
Khatumband and Pinjrakari Woodwork of Kashmir
Khatamband: A Symphony of Geometric Precision

states.caution: Historically associated with the Ladakhi royal family and ceremonial women's dress (sulma); the thigma circle appears in 12th-century Alchi murals, a Buddhist monastery context. Keep to 'inspired by Ladakhi thigma'; do not reproduce monastery imagery. Attribute to Ladakhi women dyers of Nubra and Sabu; GI-protected name, so do not call outputs 'Thigma'.

sources.title: The Fabric of Life: Nomadic Textiles from the Ladakh Himalayas
Eight traditional Ladakhi products receive GI tag

states.tradition: Lakshadweep coir and screw-pine mat weave (fallback)
states.caution: This is an honest fallback: no authoritative source documents a distinct Lakshadweep geometric mat motif vocabulary. Frame outputs as 'inspired by island coir and screw-pine mat weaves of Lakshadweep' and do not claim a named tradition. Lakshadweep's coir economy is largely rope and yarn today (PARI), with patterned mats mostly historical or emporium products. Minicoy (Maliku) has a distinct Maldivian-linked culture; do not conflate it with the Malayalam-speaking northern islands.

sources.title: Maliku Museum: Collection of Items catalogued by Vineeta Hoon & K.G. Mohammed

states.tradition: Kolam as practised in Puducherry (Tamil-region threshold kolam)
states.caution: Kolam is not unique to Puducherry; it is the Tamil tradition practised in a UT with a Tamil majority (Puducherry and Karaikal) and should be framed as 'inspired by kolam as drawn in Puducherry', not as a distinct Puducherry craft. Ritual/offering context and women's practice as for Tamil Nadu. The UT's own registered GIs (Villianur Terracotta Works, Thirukannur Papier Mache) are figurative, not geometric.
